newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Taiwan, Indonesia feature.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Taiwan, Indonesia feature.

text.p: Asian debt markets on Tuesday offered a US$50 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue for Union Bank of Taiwan as well as news of a number of Indonesian issues.
Union Bank's three-year certificates pay a margin of 27.5 basis points and, with fees, an all-in return of 32.5 basis points to top-tier managers.
"It's almost cheap. I think this issue is going to go well," predicted one trader.
Pricing compares favorably with issues for China Trust and First Commercial, she said, while acknowledging that "Union Bank isn't in the same league."
First Commercial last August issued five-year paper that paid just 23 basis points all-in. In July, China Trust launched five-year FRCDs that paid 29 basis points to the syndicate.

Details emerged on a US$150 million floating rate note issue for SMM Finance Cayman. Security is provided by a pledge of shares in Indonesian conglomerate Sinar Mas Multiartha equal to 210 percent of the outstanding principle amount of the notes.
AB Capital Markets and Peregrine Fixed Income are lead managers and bookrunners.

Peregrine Fixed Income has a couple of other Indonesian deals pending. Roadshows will begin next week for a five-year US$100 million 144a note issue for Citra Marga Nusaphala BV that is guaranteed by Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada.
Bankers said Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette and SBC Warburg are co-lead managers.
Citra Marga Nusaphala also has mandated Peregrine Sewu Securities to arrange a seven-year 250 billion rupiah bond.
Peregrine also is working on a 12 billion yen Euroyen guaranteed floating rate note issue for Indonesia's Bakrie International Finance.
In other news from Indonesia, bankers said they are still awaiting more news on the Riaupulp controversy.
Holders of some US$300 million of Riaupulp bonds have complained that a planned redemption of the bonds at 101 will cost them millions and is not necessary.
Riau Andalan Pulp is 98.9 percent owned by Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings.

Indenture forms on the outstanding Yankee bonds of Riapulp unit Rapp International Finance oblige Riaupulp to retire all of its oustanding secured debt at 101 percent of the principal amount if collateral sales exceed 25 percent of the book value of the collateral, sources said.
That trigger will be pulled if Riaulpulp sells chemical assets to related company Indorayon, a sale that still needs to be approved by Indorayon shareholders.
But bankers said there is still time for Riaupulp to amend the redemption plan because the chemicals sale is not slated to take place until the end of February.
The Riaupulp bonds were trading at a hefty premium before news of the redemption. Now, sources said there are bids at 101, but no offers as bondholders await news from the issuer.
Bankers said a couple of other Indonesian companies, notably Tri Polyta and Polysindo, have very similar covenants in bond contracts but that the companies have no plans to exercise them.

"We spoke with both of their managments and they reaffirmed that they have no plans to either sell any of their assets or redeem any of their bonds or at least sell any of the assets that are collateralized," said Keith Nilsson, associate of Asia research at Bankers Trust in Hong Kong.
He said the Riaupulp plan is "an isolated case."
Nevertheless, many bankers expect that prospective bond buyers will more closely scrutinize documentation going forward.
